messages.content: I am Tomas. I look after the little community radio studio on Thursdays. The microphone stand has developed a very theatrical squeak.
Hello, Tomas. I don't know any mechanical means of making a squeak disappear, but you could tell me about it while I'm here.
I have already checked the cable. This is the hinge complaining whenever anyone leans forward.
Then I would start by asking whether anyone has been leaning particularly hard today.
I put a note on the desk saying please stop leaning on this. Naturally I leaned on it while writing the note.
I'm sorry you had to discover that. Is there a convenient place to put the note now?
Are there repairs around your place that everyone has learned to work around?
No. I repair roofs, not the habits of people in them. I have a tool I don't use much, and I know it well enough to use it poorly. I have also discovered that I sometimes refuse to use it because it
We broadcast local notices and music. Tonight I am reading out the hours for a seed exchange.
Is tonight a useful night for enjoying a mechanical squeak?
The notices are handwritten. One of them looks as if it says bring your own goat, but I think it means coat.
I think you would know more from hearing the words in that particular sentence.
Would you correct a mistake like that as you read, or stop and admit you could not make it out?
I would stop and ask. I don't want my audience to think I've become the person who wrote the notice.
I once announced that the library would open at nine in the evening. Three people actually came.
I can't imagine a more useful evening for a library.
They were amused about it. The librarian less so.
She probably wanted to get them home before they started noticing how cold it was.
I am drinking water from a square green bottle. It makes a loud glug at exactly the wrong moment.
Could I get a picture of the bottle? I am not easily persuaded that a bottle is making an unhelpful sound simply because I am drinking from it.
What do you keep within reach when you settle down to talk?
Usually a kettle. I can't see the bottle from where I am now, so that is as good a description as I can give you.
An older volunteer here insists on doing all the labels with a ruler. I used to think that was ridiculous, but his are the only ones still readable.
I would leave the reading part to him. A bottle with a ruler on it might still have to be read.
Did somebody older than you teach you a habit that seemed fussy at the time?
Yes. I was quite impatient to be useful. I repaired roofs and became rather fond of being up on them.
No grand wisdom required. I was thinking of labels and hinges.
I like a hinge that complains about being put on too soon. It is a free ride I would not want to miss.
The next presenter has arrived early, so I have a few minutes with nothing I need to do.
Has the audience arrived?
What would you do with a free ten minutes before supper?
I would probably sit where I am now, water another kettle, and ask myself whether I was doing anything I would enjoy in the next hour.
